# Appendix J — Pattern Catalog

This catalog locates the patterns discussed in the handbook. It is an index and not a recommendation: the section named for each pattern explains when it applies and what it costs.

## J.1 Integration and Messaging

| Pattern | Problem it addresses | Section |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Request/response | The caller needs the outcome within a bounded time | 6.1.2 |
| Request-reply over messaging | A sender needs an answer without a synchronous call | 6.1.5 |
| Point-to-point channel | One owner must act on a message | 6.1.5 |
| Publish-subscribe | Any number of consumers need the same event | 6.1.5 |
| Competing consumers | Work must be shared across workers | 6.1.4 |
| Event notification | Consumers need to know that something happened | 6.1.5 |
| Event-carried state transfer | Consumers need data without calling the owner | 6.1.5 |
| Event streaming with replay | Consumers need an ordered and replayable history | 6.1.6 |
| Batch and file transfer | Volume or partner constraints rule out online calls | 6.1.7 |
| Webhook | A provider must notify a consumer of a change | 6.1.8 |
| Transactional outbox | A state change and its event must not diverge | 6.3.1 |
| Idempotent consumer | Delivery can repeat a message | 6.3.2 |
| Retry with backoff | Transient failures should not reach the caller | 6.4.1 |
| Circuit breaker | Persistent failure of a dependency should stop further calls | 6.4.1 |
| Backpressure | Producers can overwhelm consumers | 6.4.1 |
| Saga with compensation | A business transaction spans several owners | 6.4.3 |
| Dead-letter queue | Unprocessable messages must not block the flow | 6.4.4 |
| Reconciliation | Two systems may disagree after failures | 6.4.4 |
| Enterprise service bus | Many systems need shared mediation | 6.6.2 |
| Anti-corruption layer | A legacy model must not leak into a new design | 15.1.2 |

: Patterns for integration and messaging

## J.2 Application Structure and State

| Pattern | Problem it addresses | Section |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Modular monolith | Modules need boundaries without distribution | 7.1.2 |
| Microservices | Parts need independent release and scaling | 7.1.2 |
| Layered architecture | Responsibilities need a simple separation | 7.2.1 |
| Hexagonal architecture | The domain must not depend on infrastructure | 7.2.1 |
| Clean architecture | Dependencies must point toward the domain | 7.2.1 |
| CQRS | Reads and writes have different needs | 7.3.1 |
| Durable workflow | A process waits or spans long periods | 7.3.2 |
| Cache-aside | Frequent reads overload the store | 7.3.3 |
| Read-through cache | Callers should not own loading logic | 7.3.3 |
| Write-through cache | Reads must stay fresh after writes | 7.3.3 |
| Write-behind cache | Writes must be acknowledged quickly | 7.3.3 |
| Write-around cache | Rarely read writes should not occupy the cache | 7.3.3 |
| Multi-level cache | Hot data needs a fast local tier and a shared tier | 7.3.4 |
| Event sourcing | The full history of changes is a requirement | 7.3.5 |
| Bulkhead | One failure must not exhaust shared resources | 7.4.2 |
| Backend for frontend | Each client needs its own composition | 7.6.2 |
| Micro-frontends | Teams must release parts of one interface independently | 7.6.3 |

: Patterns for application structure and state

## J.3 Tenancy and Fault Isolation

| Pattern | Problem it addresses | Section |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Silo tenancy | A tenant needs dedicated resources | 7.7.1 |
| Pool tenancy | Tenants share resources to lower cost | 7.7.1 |
| Bridge tenancy | Isolation needs differ by layer | 7.7.1 |
| Deployment stamp | Groups of tenants need independent copies of the stack | 7.7.1 |
| Cell-based architecture | Failures must be contained to a subset of customers | 8.2.1 |

: Patterns for tenancy and fault isolation

## J.4 Infrastructure and Runtime

| Pattern | Problem it addresses | Section |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Backup and restore | Recovery can tolerate hours of interruption | 8.2.2 |
| Pilot light | Recovery needs a minimal running core | 8.2.2 |
| Warm standby | Recovery needs a scaled-down running copy | 8.2.2 |
| Active-active | Several regions must serve traffic together | 8.2.2 |
| Infrastructure as code | Environments must be reproducible and reviewable | 8.3.1 |
| Load balancer | Traffic must be spread among healthy instances | 8.6.3 |
| Reverse proxy | Servers need a controlled entry point | 8.6.3 |
| API gateway | APIs need policy per consumer | 8.6.3 |
| Service mesh | Service-to-service controls must be uniform | 8.7.3 |
| GitOps | Runtime state must follow a reviewed record | 8.7.4 |
| Store and forward | Devices or sites lose connectivity | 8.8.2 |

: Patterns for infrastructure and runtime

## J.5 Delivery and Evolution

| Pattern | Problem it addresses | Section |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Canary release | A change must reach a small audience first | 11.1.2 |
| Blue-green deployment | Cut-over must be immediate and reversible | 11.1.2 |
| Trunk-based development | Long-lived branches delay integration | 11.1.3 |
| Expand-migrate-contract | A schema must change without downtime | 11.2.2 |
| Feature flag | Deployment and release need to be separated | 11.2.3 |
| Strangler Fig | A legacy system must be replaced in slices | 15.1.2 |
| Consumer-driven contract testing | Providers must not break consumers without a shared environment | 14.1.2 |
| Architecture fitness function | An architectural property must keep holding on every change | 13.3.1 |
| Architecture test | The built structure must not drift from the intended dependencies and boundaries | 14.3.5 |
| Walking skeleton | The end-to-end path must be proven before the parts are built out | 13.3.2 |
| Docs as code | Documentation must change with the system it describes | 12.3.3 |

: Patterns for delivery and evolution

## J.6 Security and Data

| Pattern | Problem it addresses | Section |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Crypto-shredding | Data must be made unreadable where it cannot be deleted | 5.2.5 |
| Data product | Several consumers need governed analytical data | 5.2.6 |
| Least privilege | Access must be limited to what is needed | 9.3.1 |
| Zero Trust | Network location must not imply trust | 9.4.1 |

: Patterns for security and data

## J.7 AI Systems

| Pattern | Problem it addresses | Section |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Retrieval-augmented generation | A model must answer from governed sources | 18.3 |
| Agent loop | The steps of a task cannot be known in advance | 18.8.1 |
| Tool gateway | Agent actions need enforcement outside the model | 18.8.2 |
| Supervisor agent | Several agents need one place for policy and tracing | 18.8.3 |
| Human approval gate | High-impact actions need accountable authorization | 18.8.4 |

: Patterns for ai systems
